message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Primary Traffic Authority** | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – oversees enforcement, driver licensing, and vehicle registration. | | **Legal Framework** | Texas Transportation Code (TTC) – the main body of statutes governing road use, vehicle operation, and driver conduct. | | **Common Violations & Penalties** | • **Speeding** – fines range from $50–$500 depending on how much over the limit; points added to license.
• **Running a red light / stop sign** – $200–$400 fine, possible points.
• **Driving under influence (DUI)** – first offense: $1,000 fine, 30 days jail, 90 days license suspension; points added.
• **Seat belt violations** – $100 fine, 1 point.
• **Texting while driving** – $200 fine, 1 point.
• **Reckless driving** – $500–$1,000 fine, 30 days jail, 90 days license suspension. | | **Points System** | Texas uses a “points” system to track infractions. Accumulating 12 points within 2 years can lead to license suspension. | | **License Suspension & Revocation** | • **Suspension** – typically 30–90 days for first offenses; longer for repeat offenders.
• **Revocation** – permanent loss of driving privileges; requires re‑application and proof of rehabilitation. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections required in most counties; failure to pass can result in fines and impoundment. | | **Special Rules** | • **School bus** – must stop for all directions; failure can lead to $1,000 fine.
• **Pedestrian right‑of‑way** – drivers must yield; failure can lead to $1,000 fine.
• **Lane usage** – lane discipline rules (e.g., no left‑turn lane usage without turning). | | **Enforcement Agencies** | • DPS – state‑wide enforcement.
• Local police departments – enforce local ordinances.
• Texas Highway Patrol – enforces federal interstate laws. | | **Resources** | • **Texas DPS website** – https://www.dps.texas.gov/ (driver licensing, registration, law updates).
• **Texas Transportation Code** – https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ (full legal text).
• **Texas Courts** – https://www.txcourts.gov/ (court decisions, traffic case law).
• **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission** – https://www.tmv.org/ (vehicle registration, inspection). | --- ### How to Stay Informed 1. **Check the Texas Transportation Code** – The TTC is updated annually; you can read the full text online or consult a legal database. 2. **Follow DPS Updates** – The DPS publishes news releases and updates on new regulations or changes to existing ones. 3. **Local County Ordinances** – Some counties have additional traffic rules (e.g., speed limits on county roads). Check your county’s official website. 4. **Legal Aid & Law Libraries** – If you need detailed legal interpretation, consult a Texas attorney or visit a law library. --- #### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | *What is the maximum penalty for a DUI in Texas?* | First offense: up to 30 days jail, $1,000 fine, 90‑day license suspension. Subsequent offenses carry harsher penalties. | | *Can I get a ticket for texting while driving?* | Yes – $200 fine, 1 point. | | *Do I need to renew my license every year?* | Yes – renew every 2 years for standard licenses; renew every 4 years for commercial licenses. | | *What happens if I accumulate 12 points?* | License suspension for 30 days; after 12 points in 2 years, suspension extends to 90 days. | Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detail on any specific area—such as the exact wording of a statute, recent court cases, or how to appeal a traffic ticket!
